title: Recover leftovers without deleting unknown files
when: Uninstall or reinstall reports stale foreign-install state or partial failure
need: Setup offers Unlink and set up fresh when a checkout links to a project the chosen install lacks or the account cannot access. Project uninstall still removes the layer when the owning install is gone and warns that the commit belongs on the default branch. Machine uninstall skips Docker without a self-host install, strips Yoke's machine-wide hooks and their Codex trust from each harness's user config, removes the yoke-global skill folder and Claude link it recorded plus any parent folder it created once empty, and reverts only the harness settings it recorded writing while they still hold Yoke's value; changed settings are reported and kept, and a failed revert keeps the machine home for a retry. Machine uninstall removes Yoke-marked PATH blocks from every supported startup file, including zsh non-login and Bash SSH files, and preserves unrelated shell content; record lines right after the block, which an older CLI rewriting only the block keeps, name whether Yoke created the startup file and the folders it made for it (such as ~/.config/fish), and only those are deleted once nothing else is left, so a pre-existing empty ~/.profile survives. Machine-wide hook removal deletes a hooks file only when the ledger records Yoke created it, so a pre-existing ~/.cursor/hooks.json keeps its own content, and the summary says removed Yoke hooks from PATH (file kept) for a kept file and deleted PATH (Yoke created it; nothing else was in it) for a deleted one; Cursor folder-trust folders Yoke made go once empty. The installer and the uninstall worker remove their temporary folders once they succeed, and the summary names kept .yoke/strategy documents. Lock sidecars Yoke leaves beside harness configs (such as ~/..claude.json.yoke.lock) and the folders the relay made for its systemd unit are recorded and removed with the harness settings, deepest folder first and only once empty. Machine uninstall first runs every selected project's `yoke project uninstall --check`, and a refusal stops it before anything is removed; a project step that still fails keeps local Postgres and the self-host server its retry needs. It removes each selected project's clean Yoke lane worktrees and names the branches they leave with `git -C <checkout> branch -D <branch>`; a dirty lane, or an open lane under standalone project uninstall without --remove-lanes, refuses before any file changes or removal commit. The default-branch lookup asks the connection that registered the checkout. The final lines name uv's own removal commands for when nothing else uses uv. Reinstall replaces the owned block once per file. The hook evaluator stops before the machine home and CLI are removed; a failed stop retains both for recovery. On native Windows, a successful uninstall returns exit 0 from PowerShell and cmd, and the detached worker removes yoke.cmd.
surface: Setup project step stale-link view; uninstall step results and warnings.
review: Disposable fixtures cover exact project registration and all supported folder-trust formats, with shared and modified state preserved. Live release proof remains attached to the item.
